newsitem.title: USA: US distillate output off 200,000 bbl last week - EIA.
newsitem.headline: US distillate output off 200,000 bbl last week - EIA.

text.p: Total U.S. distillate production for the week ended January 17 was 3.1 million barrels per day (bpd), down from 3.3 million bpd the previous week, the Energy Information Administration said Thursday.

The drop in production of distillates, including heating oil and diesel, occurred in a week when U.S. distillate demand hit a one-week high for this winter of 3.7 million bpd, EIA said in its weekly distillate watch.

"Refiners have sharply lowered distillate output in reaction to a market perception that the winter crunch is over, and a number have begun turnaround maintenance before beginning the spring gasoline season," EIA said.

However, total U.S. distillate inventories at the end of last week were about 3.3 million barrels below normal, and stocks in the heating oil-dependent Northeast were 5.6 million barrels below normal for this time of year, EIA added.
Total distillate stocks fell 4.8 million barrels last week to 121 million barrels.
As expected, the Northeast saw the largest drawdown, EIA said, with distillate stocks down 2.2 million barrels to 45.6 million barrels, including a 1.9 million barrel draw of heating oil.
